dispositions.rationale: The round trip is decided by a chain the spec already pins: ACR-A23 requires the workcli rendering to equal each golden byte for byte, ACR-A27 requires each golden to parse to its entries in both consumers, and ACR-A25 holds both repositories to the same golden bytes. ACR-A26 then exercises the live installed path end to end. ACR-A25 alone is not claimed to prove the round trip.

The reciprocal source references are a maintenance device. ACR-A21, ACR-A22 and ACR-A25 observe the compatibility they protect; the parent rejected the same ground (its counterpart-marker objection) on the same basis.
Which source files a slice changes is placement, judged in PR review. It is not behaviour an acceptance check can observe; ACR-A27 observes the behaviour ACR-D7 protects.
The fixture's internal topology is implementation. ACR-D9 names both paths so ACR-A25 can compare them, and a fixture reshaped with its suites still delivers every behaviour the criteria observe.

A second marker naming the same path changes no rendering, because the last marker wins (ACR-D1). The parent promises no transaction across concurrent tracker operations (LIFE-D4, and Out of scope: cross-system transactions); ACR-A19 pins sequential replays, which is the promise made.

parts.statement: `work acceptance set` writes the exact `[work] acceptance spec: <path>` marker.
The last marker wins, absence means no named spec, and unrelated notes do not affect rendering.
For an in-root path, acceptance set resolves PATH from the invoking directory, records the root-relative reference, and can repoint it without changing text.
Both writing verbs record an outside-root path in root-relative form beginning with `..` rather than refusing it during the write.
An empty PATH records the repository root and later renders as `spec-unreadable`.
A named-spec change follows the amendment gate and trail rules, while a set changing neither text nor path writes nothing.
Delivery writes the marker with a root-relative path on the required placeholder and children.
A legacy item can acquire a named spec without changing its acceptance text.

obligations.source: ACR-D1: “The named spec is therefore a note marker, `[work] acceptance spec: <path>`”; “Two verbs write the marker”; paths are read from the working directory and recorded relative to the repository root.
obligations.statement: Items name specs through an append-only facade marker, and the two writing verbs normalize and amend that reference as specified.

parts.statement: A conventional checkout yields the same root-relative resolution from its root and subdirectories.
A linked worktree uses that worktree's root.
Absolute and lexically escaping recorded paths are refused, while lexically internal relative paths render.
Resolved symlinks may stay inside the root but may not escape it.
A spec-naming item rendered outside a repository is refused.
An item naming no spec renders without a repository root.

obligations.source: ACR-D2 defines the nearest resolved ancestor holding `.git` as the root, says a linked worktree uses its own root, lists absolute, lexical and symlink escape refusals, and permits an unnamed item to render without a root.
obligations.statement: Spec resolution is bounded by the correct repository root, including lexical and resolved-symlink confinement.

parts.statement: The successful facade envelope has data exactly containing the requested ID and markdown M.
M uses the specified headings, quoting, bullets, LF joining, terminal LF, and empty-section layout.
All description lines remain quoted and round-trip through Python splitlines behavior.
Title, item metadata, unrelated notes, spec path, and time do not enter M.
Consumers receive or write the rendering bytes without transformation.

obligations.source: ACR-D3: “`work acceptance render ID` answers in the facade's JSON envelope, whose `data` is `{"id": ID, "markdown": M}`”; it then defines every line of M and what M excludes.
obligations.statement: The render verb returns the exact facade success value and exact UTF-8 Markdown representation defined by ACR-D3.

parts.statement: Blank lines are ignored and complete citation lines resolve in order only when the item names a spec.
Non-citation lines remain text, including ID-like prose and all lines on an item naming no spec.
Ordinary generated IDs use the normalized item-ID prefix and nonblank-line position.
Generated-ID normalization removes every non-ASCII alphanumeric character and uses `ITEM` when no ASCII alphanumeric character remains.
Cited text is not recursively treated as citations, and wrapped field lines remain separate units.
Any two units yielding the same ID are refused.

obligations.source: ACR-D4 defines blank lines, citation recognition, text lines, explicit entry lines, generated `P-Tn` IDs, the `ITEM` fallback, and line-based wrapping.
obligations.statement: Acceptance-field lines are classified as citations or text, and each resulting criterion receives the required explicit or generated ID.

parts.statement: Both parsers return the fixture's entries in document order, including represented continuation, fence, empty and repeated-entry cases.
Both parsers recognize acceptance-criteria headings case-insensitively and stop at the next same-or-shallower heading.
Spec-lint's existing checks continue counting only entries with text and retain their existing results.
A citation resolves only when exactly one entry defines its ID; unresolved and ambiguous IDs are refused.
An empty entry contributes no rendered criterion, while other criteria keep field order.
Each parser copy's source names the other copy's path.
Changes to cited spec text appear on the next render without a tracker write.
A non-UTF-8 spec is unparseable and refused.

obligations.source: ACR-D5 defines the heading scope, entry and continuation grammar, empty and repeated entries, two parser copies, reciprocal source references, citation resolution, and UTF-8 requirement.
obligations.statement: Spec-lint and workcli implement the same widened criteria-entry grammar and resolution behavior.

parts.statement: Each listed render failure returns `E_RENDER` with its required cause and applicable ID or path.
An unknown item retains the existing `E_NOT_FOUND` behavior.
When failures from different rows coexist, checks run in the table's order and report the first one.
Resolution and duplicate failures are deterministic in field order.
Successful and refused rendering performs no backend mutation or file write.

obligations.source: ACR-D6 defines `E_RENDER`, detail fields, `E_NOT_FOUND`, the cause table, table-order evaluation, field-order unit checks, first-failure reporting, and no writes.
obligations.statement: Refused rendering uses the closed ACR-D6 error vocabulary, payloads, ordering and no-write behavior while preserving unknown-item handling.

parts.statement: Spec-lint and prgroom recover the required entries from every golden rendering, including hostile description shapes.
Prgroom, review-panel and ac-attack sources remain unchanged, avoiding a prgroom release and reinstall.

obligations.source: ACR-D7: “Only spec-lint's grammar changes. The verdict poster is unchanged”; it also states that review-panel and ac-attack parse no entries.
obligations.statement: Existing consumers retain their parser behavior and only spec-lint's grammar source changes in this slice.

parts.statement: Every reconciled or minted item keeps its manifest text and receives the root-relative named spec, including subdirectory invocation.
An ID-list manifest AC becomes citations while punctuation or prose remains text.
Interrupted replay adds missing markers exactly once, while completed trees, including older ones, gain none.

obligations.source: ACR-D8 requires the marker on reconciled placeholders and every manifest child, preserves manifest AC text, skips an already matching last marker, and preserves the completed-reconciliation short circuit.
obligations.statement: Spec delivery propagates the named-spec marker without replacing manifest text and converges correctly across interruption and replay.

parts.statement: Every F1 through F13 rule has at least one case, and the agents-config harness detects a missing case.
Parser and renderer results over the fixture equal `entries.json`, golden bytes and listed refusals.
The two delivered fixture copies are byte-identical and both suites pass over them.
The fixture lives at the two specified paths and retains the specified directory and file schema.
After human installation, live work output round-trips through spec-lint to the cited nonempty entries in field order.

obligations.source: ACR-D9 fixes both fixture paths, the `repo/` and `outside/` directories, the JSON and golden-file schema, and rules F1 through F13.
obligations.statement: Both repositories share a byte-identical round-trip fixture with the prescribed topology, cases and expected results.

parts.statement: Workcli render, set and delivery checks use the fake backend and injected working directories.
Agents-config checks exercise spec-lint and prgroom over fixture files without invoking the tracker.

obligations.source: Testing decisions require workcli tests to drive `main()` with a fake backend and injected working directory, materialize real symlinks and modes in a temporary directory, and avoid the tracker CLI and user's tracker.
obligations.statement: Verification uses isolated mechanical harnesses rather than the real tracker or user files.

ground.reason: ACR-D9 promises cases for the rules exercised. ACR-A24 requires only a rule label and at least one case carrying it. Its check names parser equality and unchanged lint results, neither of which establishes that a labeled case exercises the rule.

objections.objection: A fixture can claim coverage through labels while omitting the inputs and observations needed to exercise the labeled behavior.
objections.obligation: Each fixture rule F1 through F13 is exercised by a case that distinguishes its required behavior from failure.

scenario.expect: The coverage check passes because F12 has a labeled case, while no case creates a symlink and the escaping-symlink behavior remains untested.
scenario.given: A fixture case is tagged F12 but contains no symlink setup.
scenario.when: The ACR-A24 harness and its named parser and lint checks run.

ground.reason: The traceability table makes ACR-A25 a verification child for cross-repository rendering and parsing outcomes. ACR-A25 and its check require only byte-identical fixture copies and passing suites. Those artifacts can agree while the public behaviors remain wrong or unexercised.

objections.objection: Identical fixtures and green suites can be accepted as proof of cross-repository behavior without establishing the promised round trip.
objections.obligation: The delivered workcli renderer and agents-config consumers agree on the specified rendering and parsing behavior.

scenario.expect: The fixture digests match and both suites pass, while an actual workcli rendering does not round-trip through the agents-config parser.
scenario.given: Both repositories contain the same fixture and both suites omit the public integration path or share the same incorrect oracle.
scenario.when: The ACR-A25 digest and suite checks run.

ground.reason: ACR-A16 promises that both successful and refused renderings make no mutation. Its check setup names only one rendered item and does not require one successful case and one refused case.

objections.objection: Mutation on the refusal path can escape the named check.
objections.obligation: Every rendering path, including refusal paths, leaves the backend and filesystem unchanged.

scenario.expect: The successful-render snapshot and backend-log check pass, while a refused rendering writes a diagnostic file or mutates backend state.
scenario.given: A renderer is pure on success but mutates state immediately before returning E_RENDER.
scenario.when: The ACR-A16 check runs only its single successful rendering.

ground.reason: ACR-A18 combines three independently deliverable results: preserving manifest AC text, recording the root-relative spec path, and producing resolved rendering. Its check observes marker count and rendered entries but does not inspect preservation of the stored text or explicitly exercise subdirectory path recording.

objections.objection: Delivery can rewrite the manifest AC field and still pass the marker and rendering observations.
objections.obligation: Manifest-text preservation, root-relative marker recording, and downstream citation rendering require independently decidable criteria.

scenario.expect: The check sees one marker and the expected rendered entries, while the item no longer keeps its original manifest AC text.
scenario.given: Delivery replaces each manifest AC with a canonical citation line and writes a usable marker.
scenario.when: The ACR-A18 fake-backend delivery and rendering check runs.

ground.reason: ACR-D1 says a named-spec amendment passes the started-work gate when the required --why is supplied. ACR-A2 and its check establish only refusal without --why; they name no successful amendment with --why.

objections.objection: An implementation may refuse every named-spec amendment after work starts, including properly justified amendments.
objections.obligation: A started item accepts a named-spec change when the caller supplies the required justification.

scenario.expect: The refusal-without-why and repeat-no-write checks pass, while the same amendment with --why is also refused.
scenario.given: The started-work gate rejects all named-spec changes regardless of whether --why is present.
scenario.when: The ACR-A2 check exercises only the missing-why refusal and unchanged repeat.

ground.reason: ACR-D2 promises that an item naming no spec renders without a repository root. ACR-A12 covers only a spec-naming item outside a repository, and no criterion or check exercises the no-spec case outside a repository.

objections.objection: The renderer can incorrectly require a repository root for every item without failing any named check.
objections.obligation: An item with no named spec renders successfully when invoked outside a Git repository.

scenario.expect: All specified checks pass, while the no-spec item is incorrectly refused with no-repository-root.
scenario.given: The renderer looks up a repository root before checking whether the item names a spec.
scenario.when: A no-spec item is rendered outside any Git repository.

ground.reason: ACR-D6 preserves E_NOT_FOUND for an unknown item, but no acceptance criterion or check invokes rendering with an unknown item ID or decides that result.

objections.objection: The new renderer may replace the established unknown-item result with E_RENDER or another error while every listed criterion passes.
objections.obligation: Rendering an unknown item preserves the existing E_NOT_FOUND response.

scenario.expect: The listed checks pass, while the unknown item returns E_RENDER instead of E_NOT_FOUND.
scenario.given: The render verb maps every backend lookup failure to its new rendering error.
scenario.when: A caller runs work acceptance render with an unknown item ID.

ground.reason: No check observes whether acceptance set persists the named spec using the required marker spelling. Rendering can use different storage and still pass every check.

objections.objection: The implementation may omit the required `[work] acceptance spec: <path>` note written by `work acceptance set`.

scenario.expect: The item contains the exact `[work] acceptance spec: <path>` marker.
scenario.given: An item has no named-spec marker.
scenario.when: `work acceptance set ID TEXT --spec PATH` stores the path in an alternative backend location and rendering resolves it correctly.

ground.reason: The path-refusal criteria start with an already recorded path. No check exercises either writing verb with an outside-root path and observes the required root-relative `..` form.

objections.objection: A writing verb may reject an outside-root path immediately or record it in another form, even though the design requires recording it and deferring refusal to rendering.

scenario.expect: The verb records a root-relative path beginning with `..`; a later rendering refuses it.
scenario.given: A readable spec lies outside the repository.
scenario.when: `work acceptance set --spec` or `work deliver --spec` is invoked with that path and instead rejects it or stores an absolute path.

ground.reason: The what-if table commits empty PATH to a specific normalization and refusal, but no stated fixture rule or check requires that case.

objections.objection: An empty `--spec` value may receive arbitrary handling while all listed checks pass.

scenario.expect: The repository root is recorded and rendering returns `E_RENDER` with cause `spec-unreadable`.
scenario.given: The command is run inside a repository with an empty PATH.
scenario.when: `work acceptance set ID TEXT --spec ''` rejects the argument or records a different path.

ground.reason: The root and subdirectory checks cover a conventional checkout, but no check runs from a linked worktree and distinguishes its root from the main checkout or common Git directory.

objections.objection: Root discovery may choose the wrong checkout in a linked worktree.

scenario.expect: The linked worktree's own root bounds path resolution.
scenario.given: The item is rendered in a linked worktree whose `.git` entry points elsewhere.
scenario.when: The implementation treats the main checkout or Git common directory as the repository root.

ground.reason: ACR-A12 checks only the spec-naming case outside a repository. No check observes the promised behavior of an item that names no spec.

objections.objection: The renderer may unnecessarily require a repository root for tracker-only criteria.

scenario.expect: The item renders without looking for a repository root.
scenario.given: An item names no spec and the working directory has no `.git` ancestor.
scenario.when: The renderer returns `no-repository-root`.

ground.reason: The successful-render checks compare markdown bytes or parsed entries. None observes the complete success envelope, including the returned item ID and the absence of extra data members.

objections.objection: A successful render may return the right markdown in the wrong facade envelope.

scenario.expect: The success data is exactly `{"id": ID, "markdown": M}`.
scenario.given: The generated markdown equals every golden file.
scenario.when: The command returns data without `id`, with the wrong `id`, or with additional success fields.

ground.reason: ACR-A6 is checked through fixed fixture cases, while ACR-A24 requires only one F6 case. No required scenario exercises an item ID containing no ASCII letters or digits.

objections.objection: Generated IDs may fail to use the `ITEM` fallback for punctuation-only or non-ASCII item IDs.

scenario.expect: The generated criterion ID starts with `ITEM-T` and matches the criterion-ID pattern.
scenario.given: The item ID is `---` and its field contains one ordinary text line.
scenario.when: The renderer derives an empty prefix or retains disallowed characters.

ground.reason: The fixture rules do not require cases for case-insensitive heading recognition or termination at the next same-or-shallower heading. Parser equality on an unconstrained fixture does not cover those branches.

objections.objection: Either parser may use a narrower or wider section scope than ACR-D5 while satisfying every fixture check.

scenario.expect: Entries under the mixed-case acceptance heading are returned, while the bullet after the following peer heading is excluded.
scenario.given: A document contains `## Acceptance Criteria`, an entry, then `## Notes` and another criterion-shaped bullet.
scenario.when: The workcli counterpart parser is case-sensitive or continues parsing through `## Notes`.

ground.reason: Behavioral parser checks do not inspect the two source files for the required reciprocal path references.

objections.objection: The two grammar copies may omit the source-level cross-reference that the design requires.

scenario.expect: Each grammar source names the path of its counterpart.
scenario.given: Both parsers produce every expected fixture entry.
scenario.when: Their source files contain no reference to one another.

ground.reason: The refusal criteria enumerate rendering failures for known items, but none invokes the verb with an unknown item and checks preservation of `E_NOT_FOUND`.

objections.objection: An unknown item may be converted to `E_RENDER` or another error.

scenario.expect: The existing `E_NOT_FOUND` response is returned.
scenario.given: The requested item ID does not exist.
scenario.when: `work acceptance render` reports `E_RENDER` instead.

ground.reason: F7 requires first-failure behavior only for unresolved, ambiguous, and duplicate IDs. No check fixes precedence across the earlier path and file causes and later unit failures.

objections.objection: The implementation may report failures in an order different from ACR-D6 when failures from different cause classes coexist.

scenario.expect: The missing-spec failure is reported because file checks precede unit-ID checks.
scenario.given: An item names a missing spec and its field also contains two explicit units yielding the same ID.
scenario.when: The renderer checks units first and reports `duplicate-id`.

ground.reason: ACR-A27 preserves observed parser results, but no check observes the source-change boundary stated by ACR-D7 or whether a prgroom release and reinstall were introduced.

objections.objection: The slice may modify prgroom, review-panel, or ac-attack despite the decision that only spec-lint's grammar changes.

scenario.expect: Prgroom, review-panel, and ac-attack sources remain unchanged and no prgroom release is required.
scenario.given: All golden renderings still parse to the expected entries.
scenario.when: The implementation rewrites prgroom's parser without changing its fixture-visible behavior.

ground.reason: The checks consume a fixture and compare its two copies, but none fixes the required repository locations or the declared `repo/`, `outside/`, `cases.json`, `entries.json`, and `expected/` topology.

objections.objection: The fixture may be moved or reshaped while adapted suites and byte-identical copies continue to pass.

scenario.expect: Both repositories contain the fixture at the specified paths with the specified directory and JSON structure.
scenario.given: The fixture data and results are equivalent in both repositories.
scenario.when: The author moves it elsewhere or replaces its declared topology and updates the suites accordingly.

ground.reason: ACR-A3 requires one rendered bullet per citation of a nonempty entry, while ACR-A10 (with ACR-D6's duplicate-id cause) explicitly refuses 'one ID cited twice'. The same circumstance is required to render and required to refuse.

objections.objection: An item that cites the same nonempty ID twice cannot satisfy both ACR-A3 (two bullets, one per citation, in field order) and ACR-A10 (refusal with duplicate-id), so the rendering behaviour for a repeated citation is undecidable against the set.

scenario.expect: ACR-A3 expects two bullets holding AC1's text; ACR-A10 expects E_RENDER with cause duplicate-id and no rendering
scenario.given: An item names a spec that defines entry AC1 once, and its acceptance field holds two lines each citing AC1
scenario.when: the item is rendered

ground.reason: ACR-A30 states a rendering citing an empty entry 'is not refused', unqualified, while ACR-A10 and ACR-D6 refuse two units yielding one ID 'whether or not the cited entry is empty'. A repeated citation of an empty entry meets both conditions.

objections.objection: The criteria give no consistent verdict for an item that cites the same empty entry twice: ACR-A30 lets it render with no bullet, ACR-A10 refuses it as duplicate-id.

scenario.expect: ACR-A30 expects a successful rendering with no bullet for AC2; ACR-A10 expects refusal with E_RENDER, cause duplicate-id, ID AC2
scenario.given: An item names a spec holding an empty entry AC2, and its acceptance field cites AC2 on two lines
scenario.when: the item is rendered

ground.reason: ACR-A29 says 'a slice citing only an empty entry is still reported' without naming what is reported, leaving the lint verdict open: reported as a lint failure (citing an undefined criterion) or reported as informational while the lint passes.

objections.objection: The wording leaves open whether spec-lint passes or fails a spec whose slice cites only an empty entry, and each reading produces a different lint result over the same document.

scenario.expect: One reading of 'still reported' yields a failing lint (citation of an ID that defines nothing); the other yields a passing lint with the citation merely noted
scenario.given: A spec whose acceptance-criteria section holds only the empty entry '- **AC1**' and a slice heading citing only AC1
scenario.when: spec-lint runs over the spec

ground.reason: ACR-A19 pins exactly-once marker writing only across sequential replays ('A replay after an interruption...', 'A replay of a completed reconciliation...'), and the document's own what-if table answers the twice/nothing-changed questions for delivery with replays, but no criterion covers two deliver processes running at the same time, where each can observe the pre-marker state before either writes.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a delivery that writes the named-spec marker twice for the same manifest child (violating ACR-A19's 'exactly once') when two `work deliver --spec PATH` runs interleave, because both interleaved reads see no marker before either appends one.

scenario.expect: The document implies each child ends with its marker written exactly once (ACR-A19); no criterion tests the interleaved case, so a double write passes every check
scenario.given: A manifest whose expansion is in progress, with a child minted but not yet marked
scenario.when: Two `work deliver --spec PATH` processes run concurrently against the same placeholder

ground.reason: ACR-D8 says deliver writes the marker on every manifest child and skips only an item whose last marker already names that same path; it is silent on a child whose last marker names a different spec. ACR-D1 makes a named-spec change an amendment that passes the started-work gate and needs --why, but that gate is stated for `set`, and no criterion tests whether deliver's marker write repointing an already-marked child is gated, refused, or silently applied.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a silent repointing of a manifest child's named spec by `work deliver --spec`, bypassing the started-work gate and --why trail that ACR-D1/ACR-A2 require for the identical change made through `work acceptance set`.

scenario.expect: The document implies deliver writes a new marker naming B (D8 skips only a matching path); whether this amendment is gated or refused is untested by ACR-A18/ACR-A19, and any behaviour ships
scenario.given: A manifest child whose last named-spec marker names spec A (set by a human or by an earlier deliver of another manifest), with work started on the item
scenario.when: `work deliver --spec B` reconciles the same placeholder tree
